tcs.test_item:
The Audio Management software shall persist the last valid volume level independently for Entertainment and each Information source category. Following an IGN OFF/ON cycle, the software shall restore the stored volume level when the corresponding source is activated again, subject to applicable volume restoration limits

(Confirm each source category keeps its own last volume across a restart)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play an Entertainment source at a known volume step
2. Activate an Information 1 source and set a different volume step
3. Restart the head unit
4. Read the Entertainment volume step and the Information 1 volume step and record them
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment audio plays at its set step
2. The Information 1 source plays at its own step
3. The head unit restarts
4. Each source returns to the step it was left at
tcs.reasoning: 4866100 keeps the last value per source category, so the case sets two categories to different steps: a single shared slot would return one value for both and pass a one-source check.

tcs.test_item:
Upon CAN bus wake-up, the Audio Management software shall evaluate the stored Entertainment volume level before restoration. If the stored value exceeds volume step 20, the software shall limit the restored Entertainment volume to step 20; otherwise, the stored value shall be retained for restoration

(Confirm a stored volume above the wake-up limit is brought down to it)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Set the Entertainment volume to a step above the wake-up limit
2. Put the vehicle through a CAN bus sleep and wake cycle
3. Read the Entertainment volume step and record it
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment audio plays at the set step
2. The bus wakes
3. The Entertainment volume step is at the wake-up limit
tcs.design_method: 邊界值分析 (Boundary Value Analysis, BVA)
tcs.reasoning: 4866117 caps the recalled level on wake-up rather than restoring it verbatim, so the case starts above the cap. Starting below it would restore unchanged and prove nothing.

tcs.test_item:
The Audio Management software shall persist the last valid Entertainment volume level and shall restore the stored level when the audio system is initialized, when the HU transitions to a powered-up/unmuted state, or when the active Entertainment mode changes

(Confirm the Entertainment volume returns when the system comes back on)
tcs.test_procedure:

2. Switch the system off and on again
3. Read the Entertainment volume step and record it
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment audio plays at the set step
2. The system returns
3. The Entertainment volume step is the one set before
tcs.reasoning: 4866124 is the plain recall, where 4866117 at leaf 057 is the capped one. This case stays below the cap so the two are not testing the same path.

tcs.test_item:
The Audio Management software shall persistently store the current audio operating state, including volume settings, tone settings, active audio mode, last tuned media information, playback position, playback status, RND state, mute state, traffic announcement state, AF state, LOC state, and other user-configurable audio parameters before shutdown or state transition

(Confirm the current mode settings are written to storage)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play an Entertainment source with known volume, tone and mode settings
2. Trigger the sequence that stores the mode settings
3. Read the stored mode settings and record them
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment audio plays with the set values
2. The store sequence runs
3. The stored mode settings are the values set before
tcs.reasoning: Corrected to 4866466 by D-B6-01. The candidate 4866489 carries the same sentence in the Information sequence where 4866466 is the Entertainment one, and position fixes it: 130 sits at 4866465 and 132 at 4866468. Text agreement between the routes could not have caught this — the text is genuinely identical, which is the boundary package 24 section 3 records.

tcs.test_item:
During Audio Management initialization, the software shall restore all previously stored audio operating parameters from persistent storage and apply them to the corresponding audio modules

(Confirm the stored audio parameters are applied at start-up)

2. Restart the head unit
3. Read the audio parameters and record them
tcs.expected_result:
1. The audio parameters hold the set values
2. The head unit restarts
3. The audio parameters are the values stored before the restart
tcs.spec_reference: PENDING: DR-AM10 anchor withheld pending upstream confirmation of this leaf's source
tcs.remarks: PENDING: DR-AM10 the leaf describes restoration at initialisation while the object at its document position states storage; upstream to confirm the source
tcs.reasoning: Ships against a PENDING under DR-AM10. Position fixes the leaf at 4866489 — 139 sits at 4866488 and 141 at 4866490 — but that object says store where the leaf says restore at initialisation. A leaf contradicting its own source is not something either route can resolve, so the case follows the leaf and the anchor waits on upstream.

tcs.test_item:
During system initialization, the Audio Management software shall restore all previously stored user audio settings, including volume, tone, source selection, playback state, and related Audio Management configurations

(Confirm the stored mode settings come back after a source is deactivated)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play an Entertainment source with known volume, tone and mode settings
2. Activate a source that displaces it
3. End the displacing source
4. Read the volume, tone and mode settings and record them
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment audio plays with the set values
2. The displacing source becomes active
3. The displacing source ends
4. The volume, tone and mode settings are the values held before
tcs.reasoning: 4866530 recalls the stored mode settings per CFTS019-2215. The leaf frames this as system initialisation while the clause's context is recovery after a source is deactivated; package 24 rules the scenario follows the specification and lists the framing drift as a DR-AM10 sub-item, so the case is written to the deactivation path.

tcs.test_item:
After completion of the source deactivation sequence, the Audio Management software shall restore the previously stored audio settings, including volume, tone, fade, and balance values

(Confirm the settings return after the first signal source ends)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play an Entertainment source with known volume, tone, fade and balance values
2. Trigger the signal source for this sequence
3. Wait until the signal source ends
4. Read the volume, tone, fade and balance values and record them
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment audio plays with the set values
2. The signal source becomes active
3. The signal source ends
4. The four settings are the values held before
tcs.reasoning: 4866607. Four objects carry the same recall sentence, one per signal-source sub-chapter, so position rather than text fixes which one this leaf takes — package 24 section 1 settles it by bracketing with the SYS-RA order and then reading. All four settings are read because a partial restore is what the word 'settings' guards against.

tcs.test_item:
The Audio Management software shall enable Surround Sound configuration only for audio modes that support the Surround Sound feature and shall prevent the user from enabling or disabling Surround Sound for unsupported audio modes

(Confirm surround cannot be turned on for a mode that does not support it)

tcs.expected_result:

2. The audio settings open
3. Surround sound cannot be turned on
tcs.reasoning: 4866251 restricts availability by audio mode, which is a different gate from the $Surround$ configuration parameter that 098 and 099 carry: one is what the vehicle has, the other what the current mode allows.

tcs.test_item:

tcs.pre_conditions: Surround sound is available in the current audio mode

1. Select disable for surround sound in the audio settings
2. Read $SurroundOnOff$ and record it
tcs.expected_result:
1. The disable selection is accepted
2. $SurroundOnOff$ reports "OFF"
tcs.remarks: PENDING: DR-AM4 signal not found in the supplied DBC; name kept as written in CFTS019 per R-13 (g)
tcs.reasoning: 4866254 is one direction of the user control. Its counterpart is a separate object and a separate leaf, so a latch that only ever set one value would pass whichever case matched its default.

tcs.test_item:
Upon receiving $AMPSurroundSTS$ = CFG_ST, the Audio Management software shall update the HMI to indicate that the audio system is operating in Stereo Mode within the configured display response time

(Confirm the display follows the amplifier status value "CFG_ST")
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Send $AMPSurroundSTS$ = "CFG_ST"
2. Read the surround indication shown on the HMI and record it
3. Measure the time from the signal to the display update and record it
tcs.expected_result:
1. $AMPSurroundSTS$ reports "CFG_ST"
2. The HMI indicates stereo mode
3. The measured update time is at most 100 ms
tcs.remarks: PENDING: DR-AM4 signal not found in the supplied DBC; name kept as written in CFTS019 per R-13 (g)
tcs.reasoning: 4866256. Three objects carry the same sentence with three different status values, which is why the matcher scored them alike and package 22 reported a three-way collision; the value is what separates them. 097 differs again in that the amplifier reports nothing usable and the head unit assumes stereo rather than being told it. <Tdisp> is defined at Max 100 ms.

tcs.test_item:
During Audio Management initialization, the software shall evaluate the $Surround$ configuration parameter. When the parameter is configured as Present, the software shall enable the Surround Sound configuration menu and allow the user to control the Surround Sound state through the Surround_Setup.Req interface

(Confirm the menu follows the configuration when surround is Present)

2. Start the head unit
3. Open the audio settings
4. Record the state of the surround menu item
tcs.expected_result:
1. $Surround$ reports Present
2. The head unit starts
3. The audio settings open
4. The surround menu is present and accepts operation
tcs.remarks: PENDING: DR-AM4 signal not found in the supplied DBC; name kept as written in CFTS019 per R-13 (g)
tcs.reasoning: 4867601. A-AM14-b re-read the section and found three families: 4867598 and 4867599 keyed on the signal value, 4867601 and 4867602 on presence with the $Surround_Setup.Req$ path, and 4867603 and 4867604 on presence without it. 098 and 099 speak of operability, so they take the pair that names the control path; B4's 264 and 266 speak of the menu existing and take the other. The bracket says which of the two questions this row asks.
